yaa-asantewaa.s: Yaa Asantewaa was the Queen Mother of Ejisu in the Ashanti Empire, who led the War of the Golden Stool against British rule in 1900. The uprising was provoked by the British governor's demand to sit on the Golden Stool.

yahya-ibn-ibrahim.s: Yahya ibn Ibrahim was a chief of the Gudala, a Sanhaja Berber group of the western Sahara, in the eleventh century. Returning from pilgrimage to Mecca around 1040, he met the jurist Abu Imran al-Fasi in Kairouan, a contact that led to the scholar Abd Allah ibn Yasin being sent…

yam-postal-system.s: The Yam was the relay and postal system of the Mongol Empire, a network of stations supplying fresh horses, food and lodging to official messengers and travellers. It allowed information and orders to travel rapidly across the vast empire.

yamama.s: Yamama is a historical region of central Arabia, in the area of present-day Riyadh. After the death of the Prophet Muhammad it was the base of the rival prophet Musaylima.

yangtze-river.s: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and in Asia, flowing from the Tibetan plateau east to the sea at Shanghai. Its basin became China's economic heartland, producing rice, silk, tea and other goods.

yaqub-al-mansur.s: Yaqub al-Mansur was the third Almohad caliph, reigning from 1184 to 1199. He won a great victory over Castile at the Battle of Alarcos in 1195, earning the title al-Mansur, 'made victorious by God', and raided as far as the walls of Toledo.

yaqub-ibn-killis.s: Ya'qub ibn Killis was a statesman of the Fatimid Caliphate, a convert from Judaism who became the first Fatimid vizier in Egypt in the tenth century. He organised the financial and administrative system of the new Fatimid state.

yarkent-khanate.s: The Yarkent Khanate was a successor state of the eastern Chagatai realm, centred on the oasis city of Yarkand in the western Tarim Basin. The eastern khanate split around 1462 into the Yarkent and Turpan khanates.

yasa.s: The Yasa was the body of law and decrees attributed to Genghis Khan, governing military discipline, administration and social conduct among the Mongols. It served as a foundation of Mongol imperial governance.

yazdegerd-iii.s: Yazdegerd III was the last king of the Sasanian Empire, who came to the throne as a youth in the 630s. His reign saw the Arab conquest of Iran, with decisive defeats at al-Qadisiyya and Nahavand.

yazid-i.s: Yazid I was the second Umayyad caliph, reigning from 680 to 683, the son of Muawiya. His succession was contested, and his reign saw the killing of Husayn ibn Ali at Karbala in 680 and the revolt of Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.

year-name.s: A year-name was a dating formula used in early Mesopotamia, in which each year was named after a notable event of the previous year, such as a military victory or the building of a temple. Accounts of the Babylonian Empire note that Hammurabi's year-names, attached by scribes…

yejju-dynasty.s: The Yejju dynasty was an Oromo family of regional lords from Yejju in north-central Ethiopia who dominated the Ethiopian court during the Zemene Mesafint. Accounts of the Ethiopian Empire note that, while many emperors occupied the throne, real governance passed to Ras regents…

yekuno-amlak.s: Yekuno Amlak was an emperor of Ethiopia who seized power from the Zagwe dynasty in 1270. He founded the Solomonic dynasty, which claimed descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba and ruled Ethiopia, with interruptions, until 1974.

yellow-river.s: The Yellow River is the second-longest river in China, flowing from the Tibetan plateau across the north China plain to the Bohai Sea. It is considered the cradle of Chinese civilisation but is notorious for devastating floods and changes of course.

yellow-river-floods-of-1344.s: The Yellow River floods of 1344 were catastrophic floods in which the river burst its dykes and shifted its course, devastating agriculture across the north China plain. The floods destroyed agricultural production and displaced millions of people.

yellow-turban-rebellion.s: The Yellow Turban Rebellion was a large peasant uprising in China that began in 184 CE, led by the Taoist faith healer Zhang Jue and his brothers. Driven by millenarian expectations and agrarian distress, it spread across much of northern China.

yemen.s: Yemen is a region in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula, historically a centre of trade in incense and a link between Arabia, the Horn of Africa and the Indian Ocean. The Aksumite Empire extended its control over Yemen in the sixth century before being expelled by the…

yenisei-kyrgyz.s: The Yenisei Kyrgyz were a Turkic people of the upper Yenisei River region in southern Siberia. Accounts of the Gokturk Empire record that Qapaghan Qaghan conquered the Yenisei Kyrgyz and killed their qaghan in personal combat in 710.

yermak-timofeyevich.s: Yermak Timofeyevich was a Cossack leader who led an expedition across the Ural Mountains into Siberia in the 1580s, defeating the Khanate of Sibir. His campaigns from 1581 onward opened the way for Russian expansion across northern Asia.

yhwh.s: YHWH, conventionally rendered as Yahweh, is the name of the God of Israel in the Hebrew Bible. The Assyrian deportation of the population of the Kingdom of Israel had consequences for Jewish religious thought.

yiddish.s: Yiddish is a language of the Ashkenazi Jews, based on medieval German with Hebrew, Aramaic and Slavic elements and written in the Hebrew alphabet. It became the everyday language of Jewish communities across central and eastern Europe.

yijing.s: Yijing was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled by sea to India in the late seventh century, staying in Srivijaya on his journeys and visiting it in 671 CE. He studied Sanskrit there and described the kingdom as a major centre of Buddhist learning.

yin-shan.s: The Yin Shan are a range of mountains in Inner Mongolia, north of the great bend of the Yellow River. They formed a frontier zone between the Chinese plains and the steppe.

yongle-emperor.s: The Yongle Emperor was the third emperor of the Ming Empire, reigning from 1402 to 1424 after seizing the throne from his nephew. He moved the capital to Beijing, began construction of the Forbidden City and campaigned against the Mongols.

yongzheng-emperor.s: The Yongzheng Emperor was the third Qing emperor to rule China, reigning from 1722 to 1735 between the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors. He strengthened central administration, created the Grand Council and reformed taxation, curbing corruption among officials.

yoruba.s: The Yoruba are a major West African people of south-western Nigeria and neighbouring Benin, with a long tradition of urban city-states and the sacred city of Ile-Ife. The Oyo Empire was the most powerful Yoruba state, dominating the region from the seventeenth to the early…

yuan-dynasty.s: The Yuan Dynasty was the Mongol-ruled dynasty of China, proclaimed by Kublai Khan in 1271, which completed the conquest of the Southern Song in 1279. It made Beijing, then Dadu, its capital, promoted trade across Eurasia and patronised Tibetan Buddhism.

yuezhi.s: The Yuezhi were a nomadic people who lived in the region of the Gansu corridor in north-western China in the late first millennium BCE. Defeated by the Xiongnu in the second century BCE, they migrated westwards to Central Asia, where one branch later founded the Kushan Empire.

yugoslavia.s: Yugoslavia was a state of the South Slavs in the Balkans, proclaimed in 1918 as the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes from territories including former Austro-Hungarian lands. Accounts of the Austro-Hungarian Empire list it among the successor states of the empire.

yunfa.s: Yunfa was a sultan of the Hausa kingdom of Gobir and a former pupil of Usman dan Fodio. His conflict with dan Fodio's community triggered the jihad of 1804 that founded the Sokoto Caliphate.

yusuf-ibn-tashfin.s: Yusuf ibn Tashfin was the leader of the Almoravid Empire who died in 1106. He founded Marrakesh as the Almoravid capital, completed the conquest of Morocco and, at the invitation of the taifa kings, intervened in Iberia, defeating Alfonso VI of Castile at Sagrajas in 1086.

yusuf-ii.s: Yusuf II was an Almohad caliph who reigned from 1214 to 1224, succeeding his father Muhammad al-Nasir after the catastrophic defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212. He came to the throne young and ruled weakly.

yuwen-tai.s: Yuwen Tai was a general of Xianbei descent who controlled the western half of the Northern Wei after it split in 534–535, ruling Western Wei as paramount general from Chang'an. He created the fubing militia system and modelled his government on the Zhou rites.

yang-ganzhen.s: Yang Ganzhen was a powerful official of the Erhai region of Yunnan, in the former lands of Nanzhao. In 928 he overthrew Zheng Longdan, last ruler of the Da Changhe, and placed Zhao Shanzheng on the throne of the short-lived Da Tianxing, before taking power himself and founding…

yaroslav-the-wise.s: Yaroslav the Wise was Grand Prince of Kiev from 1019 to 1054, after a long war of succession among the sons of Vladimir the Great. He defeated the Pechenegs outside Kiev in 1036, built the Cathedral of Saint Sophia, founded the town of Yaroslavl and is credited with the first…

yelu-dashi.s: Yelü Dashi was a Khitan prince of the Liao dynasty who fought the Song and the Jurchen in its final years. When the Jurchen Jin destroyed the Liao in 1125 he led followers west into Central Asia, took Balasagun and proclaimed himself Gurkhan, founding the Qara Khitai.

yaqub-beg.s: Yaqub Beg was a commander from the Khanate of Kokand who took advantage of the Muslim revolts against the Qing to seize Kashgar in 1865. He built the state of Yettishar in the Tarim basin, recognised by Britain, Russia and the Ottoman Empire.

ying-bu.s: Ying Bu was a Chinese general who rebelled against the Qin dynasty and served Xiang Yu, who made him King of Jiujiang in 206 BCE. He went over to Liu Bang during the Chu–Han contention and was made King of Huainan.

yuan-shikai.s: Yuan Shikai was a Chinese general who built the modern Beiyang Army under the Qing. In 1912 he arranged the abdication of the last emperor and became President of the Republic of China, then dissolved parliament and ruled as a dictator.

yuri-dolgoruky.s: Yuri Dolgoruky was Prince of Rostov-Suzdal and, at the end of his life, Grand Prince of Kiev. A son of Vladimir Monomakh, he built up the north-eastern lands of Rus, founding towns such as Pereslavl-Zalessky and Yuryev-Polsky.

yahya-ibn-ghaniya.s: Yahya ibn Ghaniya was a leader of the Banu Ghaniya, heirs of the Almoravids, who continued his brother Ali's war against the Almohad Caliphate in Ifriqiya for about half a century. Allied with Arab tribes, he took Tunis and Mahdia around 1203 and killed his former ally…

yahya-ibn-ali-ibn-ghaniya.s: Yahya ibn Ali ibn Ghaniya was an Almoravid governor and commander in al-Andalus during the empire's collapse in the 1140s. As local rulers set up the second taifa kingdoms, he fought to hold or retake cities such as Córdoba against rebels and Christian kings.

yelu-deguang.s: Yelü Deguang, Emperor Taizong of Liao, was the second emperor of the Khitan Liao dynasty from 927. He helped Shi Jingtang overthrow the Later Tang in 936 and received the Sixteen Prefectures around Beijing in return.

yu-the-great.s: Yu the Great is the legendary Chinese ruler said to have tamed the great flood by dredging channels rather than building dams, and to have founded the Xia dynasty. Later Zhou and Han writers made him a model of the dutiful sage-king.

yunus-khoja.s: Yunus Khoja was the ruler of Tashkent in the late 18th century, who united the city's four rival quarters in the 1780s and built a short-lived independent state. He extended his authority over neighbouring Kazakh lands and the trade routes of the steppe.

yadavindra-singh.s: Yadavindra Singh was the last ruling Maharaja of Patiala, reigning from 1938, and served as Chancellor of the Chamber of Princes. He acceded to India in 1947 and in 1948 became Rajpramukh, the constitutional head, of the Patiala and East Punjab States Union, which was merged…

yaksha-malla.s: Yaksha Malla was king of the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal from 1428 to 1482, the last to rule the whole Malla kingdom from Bhaktapur. He extended its frontiers and built temples in Bhaktapur.

yakub-ii-of-germiyan.s: Yakub II of Germiyan was the last bey of the Germiyanid beylik in western Anatolia, centred on Kütahya. The Ottoman sultan Bayezid I annexed his lands in 1390, but after Timur's victory at Ankara in 1402 Yakub II was restored.

yamauchi-kazutoyo.s: Yamauchi Kazutoyo was a Japanese daimyo who served Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi and sided with Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara in 1600. As a reward Ieyasu gave him Tosa province, taken from Chosokabe Morichika.

yang-pu.s: Yang Pu was the last ruler of Wu, one of the Ten Kingdoms of southern China, and a son of its founder Yang Xingmi. He came to the throne in 920 while real power lay with the regent Xu Wen and his adopted son Xu Zhigao, and took the title of emperor in 927.

yang-tong.s: Yang Tong was a grandson of Emperor Yang of Sui, enthroned as Sui emperor at Luoyang in 618 by Wang Shichong and other officials after Emperor Yang's murder. With Wang in control, he was a figurehead during the fighting against Li Mi's Wagang army.

yang-yinglong.s: Yang Yinglong was the last hereditary chief of Bozhou, a native chiefdom in northern Guizhou ruled by the Yang family for some seven centuries. He rebelled against the Ming in 1589, a revolt counted among the Wanli Emperor's Three Great Campaigns.

yao-chang.s: Yao Chang was a Qiang general who founded the Later Qin in northern China. Serving the Former Qin, he rebelled after its defeat at the Fei River in 383, captured and killed the Former Qin ruler Fu Jian in 385, and proclaimed himself emperor at Chang'an in 386.

yaroslav-ii-of-vladimir.s: Yaroslav II of Vladimir, a son of Vsevolod the Big Nest, held Pereslavl-Zalessky from 1212 and was grand prince of Vladimir from 1238 to 1246, after the Mongol invasion. He was the father of Alexander Nevsky, born at Pereslavl.

yelu-bei.s: Yelü Bei was the eldest son of Abaoji, founder of the Khitan Liao dynasty. After the conquest of Balhae in 926 he was made ruler of Dongdan, the Eastern Khitan Kingdom set up in its lands.

yelu-chun.s: Yelü Chun was a Khitan prince of the Liao imperial clan, enthroned at Yanjing (Beijing) in 1122 by officials after Emperor Tianzuo fled from the Jurchen into the western steppe. His Northern Liao regime held the Yanjing region and repelled a Song attack, but he died within…

yelu-liuge.s: Yelü Liuge was a Khitan commander in Manchuria who rebelled against the Jurchen Jin dynasty in 1212, as Mongol attacks weakened it. Allying with Genghis Khan, he founded the Eastern Liao kingdom and ruled it as a Mongol vassal.

young-khivans.s: The Young Khivans were a reformist movement in the Khanate of Khiva, formed in the 1910s on the model of the Young Turks and the Jadid reformers of Central Asia. In 1920, allied with the Red Army, they overthrew the last khan, Said Abdullah, and the Turkmen warlord Junaid…

yuan-shao.s: Yuan Shao was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty, from a family of high officials. He led the coalition against Dong Zhuo in 190 and became master of northern China, allying with Wuhuan chiefs such as Tadun.

yuan-shu.s: Yuan Shu was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty and cousin of Yuan Shao. Holding the Huainan region, he proclaimed himself emperor of a state called Zhong in 197, which made him an outcast among the other warlords.

yuknoom-yichaak-kahk.s: Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ahk' was a king of the Kaan dynasty of the Maya, ruling from Calakmul from 686. Heir to the powerful Yuknoom Ch'een II, he maintained Kaan's network of client kingdoms, including La Corona, where a hieroglyphic stairway records his visit in 696.

yunus-khan.s: Yunus Khan was khan of Moghulistan from 1462 to 1487, a Chinggisid ruler of the Chagatai line. Raised in exile among the Timurids, he was installed with Timurid support and later held Tashkent.

yusuf-ali-kenadid.s: Yusuf Ali Kenadid was a Somali ruler who founded the Sultanate of Hobyo on the Indian Ocean coast in the 1870s. A member of the ruling house of the Majeerteen Sultanate, he fought a long war with his kinsman Boqor Osman Mahamuud before leaving to carve out a new state further…

yusuf-bey-of-the-nogai-horde.n: Yusuf Bey of the Nogai Horde
yusuf-bey-of-the-nogai-horde.s: Yusuf Bey was ruler (bey) of the Nogai Horde from 1549 to 1554, a son of Musa Bey. He opposed Muscovite expansion on the Volga, and his daughter Söyembikä was a queen of the Khanate of Kazan.

yuwen-hu.s: Yuwen Hu was a Xianbei statesman, nephew of Yuwen Tai, the strongman of Western Wei. After his uncle's death in 556 he forced the last Western Wei emperor to abdicate in 557 in favour of Yuwen Tai's son Yuwen Jue, founding the Northern Zhou.

yugoslav-partisans.s: The Yugoslav Partisans were the Communist-led resistance movement in occupied Yugoslavia during the Second World War, commanded by Josip Broz Tito. They rose in July 1941, briefly holding the Republic of Užice in western Serbia and much of Montenegro, and fought the Axis…

yaghmurasan-ibn-zayyan.s: Yaghmurasan ibn Zayyan was the founder of the Zayyanid dynasty of Tlemcen in western Algeria. As Almohad power faded he took control of the city in 1235 and soon ruled independently, fending off the Hafsids to the east and the Marinids to the west in a long reign that lasted…

yahya-al-qadir.s: Yahya al-Qadir was the last Dhu al-Nunid ruler of the Taifa of Toledo, from 1075. Weak and dependent on Alfonso VI of León and Castile, he surrendered Toledo to Alfonso in 1085 in return for help in taking Valencia, which he ruled under Castilian protection until he was killed…

yahya-ibn-ali.s: Yahya ibn Ali al-Mu'tali was a Hammudid claimant to the caliphate of Córdoba, ruling there in 1021–1023 and 1025–1026. Driven from the capital, he made Málaga his base while still claiming the title of caliph, founding the Hammudid Taifa of Málaga, and was killed in 1035…

yajaw-chan-muwaan.s: Yajaw Chan Muwaan was a Maya ruler of Bonampak in Chiapas, Mexico, in the late 8th century. Structure 1 at Bonampak, with its three rooms of painted murals showing court ceremony, battle and the presentation of captives, was created around 790 under his rule and is the…

yajaw-te-kinich-ii.s: Yajaw Te' K'inich II was a Maya king of Caracol in Belize. Allied with the Kaan dynasty of Calakmul, Caracol under his rule took part in the 'star war' that defeated Tikal in 562, beginning more than a century of Tikal's decline and Caracol's rise.

yakhshi-bey.s: Yakhshi Bey was a ruler of the Karasid beylik of north-western Anatolia, governing Pergamon in the 1330s. The traveller Ibn Battuta met him there and recorded the visit; the Karasid lands were absorbed by the Ottomans within a few years.

yala-ibn-muhammad.s: Ya'la ibn Muhammad al-Ifrani was a chief of the Banu Ifran Zenata Berbers of the central Maghreb. Allied with the Umayyads of Córdoba against the Fatimids, he founded the town of Ifgan and was killed in 958 during the western campaign of the Fatimid general Jawhar.

yamauchi-toyoshige.s: Yamauchi Toyoshige, known as Yōdō, was lord of the Tosa domain in Shikoku. In the 1860s he steered between the shogunate and the loyalists, crushing Takechi Hanpeita's loyalist party, and in 1867 he urged the shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu to return power to the emperor, a step…

yang-duan.s: Yang Duan was, according to family tradition, a man from Taiyuan who recovered Bozhou, around modern Zunyi in Guizhou, from Nanzhao forces in 876. Granted hereditary authority, he founded the Yang chieftain house that ruled the Bozhou chiefdom for more than seven centuries…

yang-maosou.s: Yang Maosou was a chief of a Di clan from the upper Han River region. In 296 he led his people to Chouchi, a flat-topped mountain near modern Xihe in Gansu, and founded the Chouchi state, which his descendants ruled with interruptions for more than two centuries.

yang-xingmi.s: Yang Xingmi was a soldier of humble origins who won control of the Huainan region between the Huai and Yangtze rivers in the 890s. Made Prince of Wu by the Tang court in 902, he founded the Wu kingdom of the Ten Kingdoms period, but after his death power passed to the general…

yang-xiuqing.s: Yang Xiuqing was a leader of the Taiping Rebellion, holding the title East King and acting as chief military and administrative commander of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. He claimed to speak with the voice of God the Father, and his growing ambition led Hong Xiuquan to have…

yao-hong.s: Yao Hong was the last ruler of the Later Qin, the Qiang-ruled state of the Yao family at Chang'an. He succeeded his father Yao Xing in 416, but in 417 the Eastern Jin general Liu Yu captured Chang'an, and Yao Hong was taken south and executed at Jiankang.

yao-xing.s: Yao Xing was the second ruler of the Later Qin, from 394 to 416. He defeated the remnants of the Former Qin and the Western Qin and ruled much of north-western China from Chang'an, where he brought the monk Kumarajiva in 401 to direct the translation of Buddhist scriptures…

yaqub-shpata.s: Yaqub Shpata was an Albanian ruler of the Despotate of Arta in Epirus, the last of the Shpata family. He succeeded Muriq Shpata and allied with the Ottomans against the Tocco family, but he was killed in 1416, and Carlo I Tocco, ruler of Ioannina, captured Arta.

yar-muhammad-khan-alakozai.s: Yar Muhammad Khan Alakozai was the vizier of Kamran Shah Durrani, ruler of the Principality of Herat. He defended Herat during the Persian siege of 1837–1838, became the real power in the state, and in 1842 killed Kamran, ruling Herat himself until his death in 1851.

yara-chobyo.s: Yara Chōbyō was an Okinawan teacher and leader of the movement for the return of the Ryukyu Islands to Japan. In 1968 he became the first chief executive of the islands elected by Okinawans under the US civil administration, and after the reversion of 1972 he was the first…

yaroslav-kachmarchyk.s: Yaroslav Kachmarchyk was a Lemko leader in the western Carpathians at the end of the First World War. In December 1918 pro-Russian Lemko assemblies, refusing to join either Poland or the West Ukrainian People's Republic, proclaimed the Lemko-Rusyn Republic at Florynka with him…

yaroslav-osmomysl.s: Yaroslav Osmomysl, meaning 'of eight minds', was Prince of Galicia from 1153 to 1187, son of Volodymyrko. Under him Galicia reached the height of its power and prosperity, extending towards the Danube, and the Lay of Igor's Campaign praised him as a mighty ruler.

yaroslav-sviatoslavich.s: Yaroslav Sviatoslavich was a Rurikid prince, son of Sviatoslav II of Kiev, who ruled Murom and Ryazan and briefly Chernigov. His descendants formed the ruling lines of the north-eastern lands of Murom and Ryazan, which separated into two principalities around 1129.

yashovarman-of-kannauj.s: Yashovarman was a king of Kannauj in northern India in the early 8th century, who restored the city's power after the collapse of Harsha's empire. He patronised the playwright Bhavabhuti and the poet Vakpatiraja, whose Prakrit epic Gaudavaho celebrates his campaigns, but he…

yashovarman-chandela.s: Yashovarman was the Chandela king who made his dynasty a regional power in Bundelkhand in the mid-10th century, capturing the fortress of Kalinjar from the Gurjara-Pratiharas. He built the Lakshmana temple at Khajuraho, and his son Dhanga became the first fully independent…

yashwant-rao-holkar.s: Yashwant Rao Holkar was the Maratha ruler of Indore from 1799 to 1811. He defeated the Scindias and the Peshwa at Poona in 1802, and in 1804–1805 fought the British East India Company, routing Colonel Monson's column in 1804 before making peace at Rajghat in 1805.

yashwant-rao-holkar-ii.s: Yashwant Rao Holkar II was the last ruling Maharaja of Indore, from 1926. He acceded to India in 1947, and when Indore merged into Madhya Bharat in 1948 he served as its Uprajpramukh, deputy to Jivajirao Scindia of Gwalior, until the union joined Madhya Pradesh in 1956.

yaxha-nakum-naranjo-national-park.s: Yaxha-Nakum-Naranjo National Park is a protected area in the Petén department of northern Guatemala. It contains the Maya cities of Yaxha, Nakum and Naranjo, among other sites; protection was extended to Naranjo after heavy looting of its stelae in the 20th century.

yazaman-al-khadim.s: Yazaman al-Khadim was a eunuch commander who governed the frontier city of Tarsus in Cilicia from 882 until his death in 891. He led repeated land and sea raids against the Byzantine Empire and resisted the Tulunids of Egypt for a time before accepting their authority.

years-of-lead-italy.s: The Years of Lead (anni di piombo) were a period of political violence in Italy from the late 1960s to the 1980s. Far-left groups such as the Red Brigades and neo-fascist groups carried out bombings, shootings and kidnappings, including the Piazza Fontana bombing of 1969, the…

years-of-lead-morocco.s: The Years of Lead in Morocco were the decades of state repression under King Hassan II, from the 1960s to the late 1980s. Opponents, including leftists, Islamists, Sahrawis and suspected plotters after the coup attempts of 1971 and 1972, faced arrest, torture, disappearance…

yelu-xuedu.s: Yelü Xuedu was the son of Yelü Liuge, the Khitan leader who founded the Eastern Liao in Manchuria in 1213 as an ally of the Mongols. After his father's death in 1220 he and his mother governed the kingdom as hereditary vassals of the Mongol Empire, serving the Mongols in their…

yeon-gaesomun.s: Yeon Gaesomun was a Goguryeo general and statesman who seized power in a coup in 642, killing King Yeongnyu and placing King Bojang on the throne while ruling as military dictator. He resisted Tang invasions under Emperor Taizong, including the siege of Ansi fortress in 645.

yeshwantrao-ghorpade.s: Yeshwantrao Ghorpade was the last ruling raja of the princely state of Sandur in southern India, succeeding in 1928. He introduced reforms including a representative assembly and public services, and acceded to India in 1947 before Sandur merged into Madras Province in 1949.

yevhen-petrushevych.s: Yevhen Petrushevych was a Ukrainian lawyer and politician from Galicia, a deputy in the Austrian parliament, who became president of the Ukrainian National Council of the West Ukrainian People's Republic in 1918. In 1919 he was named dictator during the war with Poland.

yevgenia-bosch.s: Yevgenia Bosch was a Bolshevik revolutionary who served as People's Secretary of Internal Affairs in the Soviet government of Ukraine formed at Kharkiv in December 1917, and is often described as the first woman to head a modern government. She took part in the Civil War as a…

yichaak-bahlam.s: Yich'aak B'ahlam was a Classic Maya king of Ceibal, in the Petexbatun region of Guatemala. In 735 he was captured by Ruler 3 of Dos Pilas, an event recorded on Dos Pilas monuments, and Ceibal became a subordinate of the Petexbatun kingdom until its collapse later in the 8th…

yin-rugeng.s: Yin Rugeng was a Chinese official, educated in Japan, who in November 1935 declared eastern Hebei autonomous from the Nationalist government and headed the Japanese-backed East Hebei Autonomous Government at Tongzhou. The regime ended after the Tongzhou mutiny of 1937 and was…

ymer-prizreni.s: Ymer Prizreni was an Albanian Ottoman official and leader of the League of Prizren, formed in 1878 to resist the transfer of Albanian-inhabited lands to Montenegro, Serbia and Greece. He headed the league's provisional government in 1881, before the Ottoman army suppressed the…

yohannes-iv.s: Yohannes IV was Emperor of Ethiopia from 1872 to 1889, a Tigrayan noble born Kassa Mercha who gained power with British arms after the fall of Tewodros II. He defeated Egyptian invasions at Gundet and Gura in 1875 and 1876 and resisted Italian expansion.

yongli-emperor.s: The Yongli Emperor, Zhu Youlang, was the last emperor of the Southern Ming, enthroned at Zhaoqing in 1646. Backed for a time by former rebel armies under Li Dingguo, he held parts of southern and south-western China against the Qing, then fled to Burma in 1659.

young-bukharans.s: The Young Bukharans were a reformist movement in the Emirate of Bukhara, influenced by the Jadid movement and the Young Turks, who sought modern education and constitutional limits on the emir. Persecuted by Emir Alim Khan, many allied with the Bolsheviks, and in 1920 they…

yue-fei.s: Yue Fei was a Southern Song general who led campaigns against the Jurchen Jin dynasty and its client state of Qi in the 1130s, recovering territory north of the Yangtze. Opposed to the peace policy of Emperor Gaozong and the chancellor Qin Hui, he was recalled, imprisoned and…

yue-yi.s: Yue Yi was a general of the Warring States period who served King Zhao of Yan. In 284 BCE he led an alliance of states against Qi, took its capital Linzi and overran almost all of the kingdom.

yuki-hideyasu.s: Yuki Hideyasu was the second son of Tokugawa Ieyasu, adopted first by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and then by the Yuki family. After the Battle of Sekigahara his father gave him Echizen province in 1601, where he founded the domain later known as Fukui and rebuilt Kitanosho castle.

yunus-al-harfush.s: Yunus al-Harfush was the most powerful emir of the Shia Harfush family, who held Baalbek and the Beqaa valley under the Ottomans. He was at first an ally of the Druze emir Fakhr al-Din II, but the two later became rivals, and Fakhr al-Din's forces took Baalbek.

yunus-ibn-ilyas.s: Yunus ibn Ilyas was a 9th-century ruler of the Barghawata, a Berber confederation on the Atlantic plains of Morocco. According to al-Bakri he openly proclaimed the religion of his grandfather Salih ibn Tarif and spread it by force, waging wars against neighbouring tribes.

yuri-gagarin.s: Yuri Gagarin was a Soviet pilot and cosmonaut who became the first human in space on 12 April 1961, orbiting the Earth once in Vostok 1, launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The flight made him a world celebrity and a symbol of Soviet technical achievement in…

yuri-yaroslavich-of-turov.s: Yuri Yaroslavich was a Rurikid prince, a grandson of Sviatopolk II of Kiev, who established himself in Turov in the late 1150s and resisted attempts by the princes of Kiev to remove him. He made Turov an independent principality with its own dynasty, whose branches later ruled…

yury-sviatoslavich.s: Yury Sviatoslavich was the last independent prince of Smolensk. Driven out when Vytautas of Lithuania took the city in 1395, he regained it with Ryazan's help in 1401, but Vytautas besieged Smolensk again and annexed it in 1404.

yusuf-adil-shah.s: Yusuf Adil Shah was the founder of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur. A governor of the Bahmani Sultanate, he declared independence around 1490 as Bahmani power broke apart.

yusuf-al-mutaman-ibn-hud.s: Yusuf al-Mutaman ibn Hud was the Hudid king of the Taifa of Zaragoza from 1081 to 1085, son of Ahmad I al-Muqtadir. A mathematician, he wrote the Kitab al-Istikmal, a large treatise on geometry studied in later centuries.

yusuf-al-muzaffar.s: Yusuf al-Muzaffar was a son of Sulayman ibn Hud, founder of the Hudid dynasty, who on his father's death in 1046 took Lleida and its region as an independent taifa kingdom. He fought a long war against his brother Ahmad al-Muqtadir of Zaragoza, who eventually absorbed Lleida…

yusuf-dey.s: Yusuf Dey was dey of Ottoman Tunisia from 1610 to 1637, the most powerful official of the regency in his time. He welcomed Morisco refugees expelled from Spain, who founded and settled towns such as Testour, and he encouraged corsairing and trade.

yusuf-ibn-abil-saj.s: Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj was the Sajid emir of Azerbaijan, ruling as a largely independent Abbasid governor from 901. He invaded Armenia, captured King Smbat I and had him executed in 914, and supported rival Armenian princes.

yusuf-ibn-ahmad-al-bitruji.s: Yusuf ibn Ahmad al-Bitruji was a local leader in south-western al-Andalus who seized Niebla in 1145, during the revolts against the Almoravids begun by Ibn Qasi in the Algarve. He ruled the town as a short-lived independent taifa before submitting to the Almohads, who soon…

yusuf-karamanli.s: Yusuf Karamanli was pasha of Tripoli from 1795 to 1832, the most powerful ruler of the Karamanli dynasty. He drew wealth from corsairing and tribute from European states, and his demands on the United States led to the First Barbary War of 1801 to 1805.

yusuf-qadir-khan.s: Yusuf Qadir Khan was a ruler of the Kara-Khanid Khanate based at Kashgar. He completed the conquest of the Buddhist Kingdom of Khotan around 1006, extending Islam in the Tarim Basin, and later became supreme khan.

yusuf-shah-chak.s: Yusuf Shah Chak was sultan of Kashmir, reigning in 1579 and again from 1580 to 1586, and one of the last rulers of the Chak dynasty. He is remembered with his wife, the poet Habba Khatun.

yusup-abdrakhmanov.s: Yusup Abdrakhmanov was a Kyrgyz communist who headed the government of the Kirghiz Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic from 1927 to 1933. He pressed for greater autonomy and opposed some harsh collectivisation measures, was accused of nationalism and removed, and was arrested…

yuwen-jue.s: Yuwen Jue was the first ruler of the Northern Zhou, son of the Western Wei regent Yuwen Tai. In 557 his cousin Yuwen Hu forced the last Western Wei emperor to abdicate in his favour, and he took the archaic title Heavenly King of Zhou.

yuwen-yidougui.s: Yuwen Yidougui was the last chief of the Yuwen Xianbei, a confederation in western Liaoning. In 344 he was defeated by Murong Huang of the Former Yan, fled into the steppe and died there, and his people were absorbed and resettled.

yola.s: Yola is a town in north-eastern Nigeria near the Benue River and the capital of Adamawa State. Modibbo Adama founded it in 1841 as the capital of the Adamawa Emirate, the large Fulani state that paid tribute to the Sokoto Caliphate.

yasodharman.s: Yasodharman was a ruler of Malwa in central India in the early 6th century, generally assigned to the Aulikara dynasty. His inscriptions at Mandsaur claim that he defeated the Alchon Hun king Mihirakula, around 528, and ruled lands from the Himalayas to the sea.

yamanaka-yukimori.s: Yamanaka Yukimori, also known as Yamanaka Shikanosuke, was a samurai retainer of the Amago clan of Izumo. After the Mōri conquered the Amago in 1566 he led repeated attempts to restore the clan, latterly with the support of Oda Nobunaga.

yesilirmak.s: The Yeşilırmak, the ancient Iris, is a river of northern Anatolia, Turkey, flowing past Tokat and Amasya to the Black Sea east of Samsun. Its valley, with that of its tributary the Lycus (Kelkit), formed the heartland of the Hellenistic Kingdom of Pontus, whose royal tombs are…

yewe.s: Yewe is a secret religious order of the Ewe of south-eastern Ghana and Togo, devoted to the thunder god Xevieso and related deities. Its initiates took new names, followed strict rules and used a language of their own, and the order became a powerful society that influenced…

yale-university.s: Yale University is a private research university in New Haven, Connecticut, founded in 1701 and one of the oldest institutions of higher learning in the United States. Its archaeologists have led major excavations in the Near East, including Harvey Weiss's work from 1979 at…

yaqub-ibn-al-layth-al-saffar.s: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth al-Saffar was the founder of the Saffarid dynasty in Sistan in eastern Iran. A coppersmith turned leader of local volunteer fighters, he seized Zaranj in 861 and conquered much of Iran and Afghanistan, overthrowing the Tahirids at Nishapur in 873.

yaqub-aq-qoyunlu.s: Ya'qub was ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu confederation from 1478 to 1490, a son of Uzun Hasan. From his capital at Tabriz he presided over a brilliant Persianate court that patronised poets and painters, and his forces helped defeat the Safavid leader Shaykh Haydar in 1488.

yusuf-al-azma.s: Yusuf al-Azma was a Syrian army officer and war minister of the Arab Kingdom of Syria. Trained in the Ottoman army, he refused to accept the French ultimatum of July 1920 without a fight and led a small force against the French at Maysalun, where he was killed on 24 July 1920.

yamani.s: Yamani was a usurper who seized the throne of the Philistine city of Ashdod around 712 BCE after the Assyrians had deposed its king. He led a revolt against Assyria in hope of Egyptian support, but when Sargon II's army arrived he fled to Kush, whose king later handed him over…

yodo-dono.s: Yodo-dono, born Chacha, was the eldest daughter of Azai Nagamasa and Oichi and became a consort of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. She bore his heir, Toyotomi Hideyori, and after Hideyoshi's death led the Toyotomi faction at Osaka Castle.

yakubu-of-bauchi.s: Yakubu was the founder and first emir of Bauchi in northern Nigeria. A Gerawa scholar and student of Usman dan Fodio, he was the only one of the original flag-bearers of the Sokoto jihad who was not a Fulani.

york.s: York is a historic city in North Yorkshire, England, where the Ouse and the Foss meet. Founded by the Romans in 71 CE as the legionary fortress of Eboracum, it was where Constantine the Great was proclaimed emperor in 306.

yamunanagar-district.s: Yamunanagar is a district in the north-east of Haryana, India, on the west bank of the Yamuna River, formed in 1989 from part of Ambala district. Its headquarters, the city of Yamunanagar with the adjoining town of Jagadhri, is an industrial centre known for plywood, paper and…

yazid-ibn-al-muhallab.s: Yazid ibn al-Muhallab was an Arab general and governor of the Umayyad Caliphate from the Azd tribe. As governor of Iraq and Khurasan under the caliph Sulayman, he conquered Jurjan in 716 but was defeated in Tabaristan by the Dabuyid ispahbad Farrukhan.

yamasee.s: The Yamasee were a Native American people of the coastal region of present-day Georgia and South Carolina. Allied with the English of Carolina, they raided Spanish Florida and its Native peoples for captives in the late 17th and early 18th centuries.

yahuarcocha.s: Lake Yahuarcocha is a lake near Ibarra in Imbabura province, northern Ecuador. Its name means 'lake of blood' in Quechua: tradition holds that the Inca ruler Huayna Capac massacred thousands of Caranqui and Cayambi warriors there in the late 15th century, staining its waters red.

yaqub-shah-chak.s: Yaqub Shah Chak was the last independent sultan of Kashmir, son of Yusuf Shah Chak. After his father surrendered to the Mughal emperor Akbar's army in 1586, Yaqub continued the resistance from the hills for several years before submitting in 1589.

yashastilaka.s: The Yashastilaka is a Sanskrit romance in mixed prose and verse by the Jain scholar Somadeva Suri, completed in 959 at the court of the Vemulavada Chalukyas. It tells the story of King Yashodhara and his rebirths to teach the Jain doctrine of non-violence, and includes a long…

yudhishthira.s: Yudhishthira is the eldest of the five Pandava brothers in the Mahabharata, the son of Kunti and, in the epic, of the god Dharma. Famed for his devotion to truth and righteousness, he lost his kingdom and his brothers' freedom in a rigged game of dice, and after the…

yamagata-aritomo.s: Yamagata Aritomo (1838–1922) was a Japanese soldier and statesman from the Chōshū domain, regarded as the father of the modern Japanese army. He introduced conscription in 1873, commanded in the First Sino-Japanese War and twice served as prime minister, in 1889–91 and 1898–1900.

yamaguchi-prefecture.s: Yamaguchi Prefecture is the westernmost prefecture of Honshu, Japan, with its capital at Yamaguchi city and its largest city at Shimonoseki. It was formed in 1871 from the Chōshū domain of the Mōri clan, covering the old provinces of Suō and Nagato.

yoshida-shoin.s: Yoshida Shōin (1830–1859) was a samurai teacher and thinker of the Chōshū domain. He tried to stow away on one of Commodore Perry's ships in 1854 to study the West and was imprisoned.

yaxuna.s: Yaxuná is an ancient Maya site in the centre of the Yucatán peninsula, about 20 kilometres south of Chichén Itzá. Settled from the Preclassic period, it was linked to Cobá in the Classic period by a raised causeway (sacbe) about 100 kilometres long, one of the longest Maya roads.

yucatan-peninsula.s: The Yucatán Peninsula is a low limestone platform in south-eastern Mexico and northern Central America, separating the Gulf of Mexico from the Caribbean Sea. It is divided among the Mexican states of Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo, together with Belize and northern Guatemala.

yamparika.s: The Yamparika, or Yap Eaters, named after a root they gathered, were the northernmost division of the Comanche. They ranged along the Arkansas River in present-day Colorado and Kansas and traded and fought with the Cheyenne, Arapaho and Kiowa.

yax-pasaj-chan-yopaat.s: Yax Pasaj Chan Yopaat was the sixteenth ruler of the Maya city of Copán, in present-day Honduras, who took the throne in 763. He commissioned Altar Q, which portrays all sixteen kings of the dynasty and shows the founder, K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo', handing him authority.

yolande-duchess-of-lorraine.s: Yolande of Anjou was a daughter of René of Anjou who inherited the Duchy of Lorraine in 1473. Her marriage to Ferry II of Vaudémont, son of René's old rival Antoine, reconciled the two branches of the house of Lorraine, and their son René II united Vaudémont with the duchy.

yagibasan.s: Yağıbasan was a Danishmendid emir, a son of Gümüştekin Gazi, who ruled from Sivas from about 1142 to 1164. He fought the Byzantines and the Seljuks of Rum and supported rivals of the Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan II.

yonezawa.s: Yonezawa is a city in the south of Yamagata Prefecture in northern Japan. The Date clan made it their seat in 1548, and from 1601 it was the castle town of the Uesugi clan, whose lord Uesugi Harunori (Yōzan) reformed the domain's finances in the 18th century.

yizhou-commandery.s: Yizhou Commandery was a commandery created by the Han dynasty in 109 BCE on the lands of the Dian kingdom in present-day Yunnan, China. Emperor Wu set it up after Dian submitted, but allowed the Dian king to keep his title and gave him a gold seal.

yalu-river.s: The Yalu River forms much of the border between North Korea and China, flowing about 790 kilometres from Mount Paektu to the Yellow Sea. Its middle valley was the heartland of Goguryeo, whose capital at Gungnae lay on its bank, and later Korean states treated it as their…

ypati.s: Ypati is a village in Phthiotis, central Greece, on the slopes of Mount Oeta above the Spercheios valley. As ancient Hypata it was the chief town of the Aenianes, and in the Middle Ages, as Neopatras, it was the seat of the rulers of Thessaly and from 1319 the capital of the…

yuhwa.s: Yuhwa is the mother of Jumong, the founder of Goguryeo, in Korean legend. Described as the daughter of the river god Habaek, she was taken in by King Geumwa of Eastern Buyeo and gave birth to Jumong.

yusuf-balasaguni.s: Yusuf Balasaguni was a Turkic poet and statesman from Balasagun, in modern Kyrgyzstan, under the Kara-Khanid Khanate. Around 1069 he completed the Kutadgu Bilig, a verse mirror for princes, and presented it to the ruler at Kashgar, who rewarded him with the title Khass Hajib,…

yanji.s: Yanji is a city in Jilin province, north-east China, and the capital of the Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture, near the borders with North Korea and Russia. The area lay in the old Jurchen homeland, and the capital of Puxian Wannu's Eastern Xia stood nearby in the early…

yaqut-al-hamawi.s: Yaqut al-Hamawi was an Arabic geographer and biographer of Byzantine Greek birth who was enslaved as a boy, educated in Baghdad and later freed. Travelling widely as a merchant and copyist, he compiled the Mu'jam al-Buldan, a great alphabetical dictionary of places, and a…

yves-devreux.s: Yves d'Évreux was a French Capuchin friar who served in the colony of Equinoctial France on the island of Maranhão in Brazil from 1612. His account of the colony and of the Tupinambá continues that of Claude d'Abbeville, but its printing was suppressed in 1615 after France…

yerevan.s: Yerevan is the capital and largest city of Armenia, on the Hrazdan river within sight of Mount Ararat. Its history begins with the Urartian fortress of Erebuni, founded in 782 BCE.

yang-di-pertuan-agong.s: The Yang di-Pertuan Agong is the head of state of Malaysia, a constitutional monarch elected for a five-year term by the Conference of Rulers from among the nine hereditary rulers of the Malay states. The office was created at independence in 1957, when Tuanku Abdul Rahman of…

yaounde.s: Yaoundé is the capital of Cameroon, set on hills in the centre-south of the country. It began as a German military and research station founded in 1889, became the capital of French-ruled Cameroon in the 1920s and has been the capital of independent Cameroon since 1960.

yanam.s: Yanam is a small town on the Godavari delta in south-east India, enclosed by Andhra Pradesh. A French trading post from the 1720s, it remained part of French India until 1954, when it was transferred de facto to India, a transfer made legal in 1962.

yokoi-shonan.s: Yokoi Shōnan was a Japanese Confucian scholar and political reformer from the Kumamoto domain. Invited to Fukui by Matsudaira Yoshinaga in 1858, he promoted trade, Western technology and government by council, and his ideas influenced the Charter Oath of 1868.

yuri-kimimasa.s: Yuri Kimimasa was a samurai of the Fukui domain and a financial official of the early Meiji government. A follower of Yokoi Shōnan, he reformed Fukui's finances, and in 1868 he wrote the first draft of the Charter Oath, which set out the principles of the new government.

yugurs.s: The Yugurs, also called Yellow Uyghurs, are an ethnic group of about 14,000 people living mainly in Sunan Yugur Autonomous County in Gansu, China. They are commonly regarded as descendants of the Ganzhou Uyghurs, who settled in the Hexi Corridor after the fall of the Uyghur…

yerba-mate.s: Yerba mate is a holly, Ilex paraguariensis, native to the forests of Paraguay, southern Brazil and north-eastern Argentina, whose dried leaves are steeped to make the caffeinated drink mate. The Guaraní drank it before the Spanish conquest, and in colonial times it became…

yuri-igorevich-of-ryazan.s: Yuri Igorevich was Prince of Ryazan when Batu's Mongol army invaded north-eastern Rus' in the winter of 1237. Having refused the Mongols' demand for a tenth of everything, he sought help from Vladimir in vain, and he was killed with his family when Ryazan fell after a short…

yaroslav-of-tver.s: Yaroslav Yaroslavich was the first Prince of Tver, from about 1247, and Grand Prince of Vladimir from 1264 to 1271. A younger brother of Alexander Nevsky, he founded the dynasty that ruled Tver until 1485 and as grand prince clashed with Novgorod, which accepted him only under…

yankton-sioux.s: The Yankton, or Ihanktonwan, are one of the seven divisions of the Oceti Sakowin, speaking the Dakota language and long grouped with the Yanktonai as the middle Sioux. In the 18th century they lived along the Missouri River in present-day South Dakota and Iowa, hunting bison…

yanktonai.s: The Yanktonai, or Ihanktonwana, are one of the seven divisions of the Oceti Sakowin, closely related to the Yankton and speaking a Dakota dialect. In the 18th and 19th centuries they ranged over the plains of the eastern Dakotas, between the Missouri and the Red River of the…

yeshe-o.s: Yeshe-Ö was a king of Guge in western Tibet in the late 10th century who became a monk and devoted his reign to restoring Buddhism. He founded Tholing Monastery in 996 and sent young Tibetans, including Rinchen Zangpo, to study in Kashmir.

yau-bidi.s: Yau-bidi, also called Ilu-bidi, was the last king of Hamath, who seized power and in 720 BCE led a revolt against Assyria with Arpad, Damascus, Samaria and other cities. Sargon II defeated him at Qarqar, had him flayed, and made Hamath an Assyrian province, deporting many of…

yasinia.s: Yasinia is a mountain settlement in Zakarpattia oblast, western Ukraine, near the source of the Tisza in the Carpathians. Formerly part of the Kingdom of Hungary, it was the centre of the short-lived Hutsul Republic of 1918-1919, until Romanian troops occupied it in June 1919.

yusuf-al-fihri.s: Yusuf al-Fihri was governor of al-Andalus from 747 to 756, a member of the Fihrid family descended from Uqba ibn Nafi. He ruled largely independently as the Umayyad Caliphate collapsed.

yorubaland.s: Yorubaland is the cultural homeland of the Yoruba people, covering south-western Nigeria and parts of Benin and Togo. It held many kingdoms, among them Ife, regarded as the place of origin, and the Oyo Empire, which dominated the region from the 17th to the early 19th century.

yalunka.s: The Yalunka, or Jalonke, are a Mande-speaking people of the Futa Jallon highlands of Guinea and neighbouring Sierra Leone and Mali, closely related to the Susu. They held the highlands, which take their name from them, until the Muslim Fulbe jihad of the early 18th century…

yodo-river.s: The Yodo River is a river of the Kansai region of Japan, flowing from Lake Biwa past Kyoto to Osaka Bay. For centuries it was the main water route between the capital and the port of Osaka.

yahya-khan.s: Yahya Khan was a Pakistani army general who succeeded Ayub Khan as president and chief martial law administrator in 1969. He held Pakistan's first general election in 1970, but when the Awami League won a majority, he launched a military crackdown in East Pakistan in 1971.

yeongjo-of-joseon.s: Yeongjo was the 21st king of Joseon Korea, ruling from 1724 to 1776, the longest reign of the dynasty. He pursued a policy of impartiality, tangpyeong, to curb factional strife at court, reduced the military cloth tax and promoted Confucian learning.

yi-sun-sin.s: Yi Sun-sin was a Korean admiral who led Joseon's navy against the Japanese invasions of 1592 to 1598. Using turtle ships and panokseon warships, he won victories such as Hansan Island in 1592 and Myeongnyang in 1597 that cut Japanese supply lines.

yahya-ibn-abdallah.s: Yahya ibn Abdallah was an Alid, a descendant of the Prophet through al-Hasan, who survived the failed Alid revolt at Fakhkh in 786. Around 791 he raised a rebellion in Daylam with the support of the local Justanid king, but surrendered to the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid on…

yamashina-hongan-ji.s: Yamashina Hongan-ji was the head temple of the True Pure Land school of Japanese Buddhism, built by Rennyo at Yamashina, east of Kyoto, and completed around 1483. A fortified temple town grew around it, from which the sect's leaders directed their followers, including the…

yazd.s: Yazd is a desert city in central Iran, famed for its mud-brick old town, windcatchers and underground qanat water channels, and as a centre of Zoroastrianism. In the Middle Ages it was ruled by Kakuyid princes, atabegs and the Muzaffarid dynasty, and Marco Polo described its…

yaska.s: Yaska was an ancient Indian grammarian and author of the Nirukta, the oldest surviving treatise on Sanskrit etymology and the interpretation of Vedic words. Usually dated to around the 5th century BCE, before Panini, he discussed how words derive from verbal roots.

yuzhno-sakhalinsk.s: Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk is the capital of Sakhalin Oblast in the Russian Far East. Founded by Russians as the village of Vladimirovka in 1882, it was rebuilt by the Japanese as Toyohara, capital of Karafuto Prefecture, from 1908.

yaghma.s: The Yaghma were a Turkic tribe of Central Asia, living in the 10th century around Kashgar and the western Tarim Basin and associated with the Toquz Oghuz. Together with the Chigils and Karluks they formed the core of the Kara-Khanid Khanate, and some historians trace the…

yafa.s: The Yafa are a tribal confederation of the highlands north-east of Aden in southern Yemen. In the early 18th century they threw off the rule of the Qasimid imams and formed the Upper and Lower Yafa sultanates.

yoshino-nara.s: Yoshino is a mountain town in Nara Prefecture, Japan, famous for the cherry trees of Mount Yoshino and for its shrines and temples on the pilgrimage routes of the Kii Mountains. In 1336 Emperor Go-Daigo fled there with the imperial regalia and set up the Southern Court, which…

yuri-horlis-horsky.s: Yuri Horlis-Horsky was a Ukrainian officer and writer who fought for the Ukrainian People's Republic and with the insurgents of Kholodny Yar against the Bolsheviks. In exile he wrote the memoir Kholodny Yar, first published in Lviv in 1934, a vivid account of the partisan…

yuasa-wakayama.s: Yuasa is a coastal town in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, on the Kii Peninsula, traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Japanese soy sauce. According to tradition the method grew from the making of Kinzanji miso, brought from China by the monk Kakushin in the 13th century,…

yervandashat.s: Yervandashat was an ancient Armenian city at the confluence of the Araxes and Akhurian rivers, founded by the Orontid king Orontes IV around the end of the 3rd century BCE as his new capital in place of Armavir. It remained a royal city until Artaxias I moved the capital to…

yeavering.s: Yeavering, in Northumberland, England, is the site of Ad Gefrin, a royal residence of the 7th-century kings of Bernicia and Northumbria below the hillfort of Yeavering Bell. Excavations from 1953 revealed great timber halls and a wedge-shaped wooden grandstand for assemblies.

yariri.s: Yariri was a regent of Carchemish in the early 8th century BCE, ruling for the young prince Kamani. His Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions, carved on sculpted reliefs at Carchemish, boast that his fame reached Egypt, Babylon and other lands and that he knew several scripts and…

ya-na.s: Ya Na is the title of the king of Dagbon, the kingdom of the Dagomba in northern Ghana, who reigns from Yendi. The kingship rotates among royal lines, and candidates must first hold one of the senior gate chieftaincies, such as Karaga, Savelugu or Mion.

yendi.s: Yendi is a town in the Northern Region of Ghana, the capital of the Dagomba kingdom of Dagbon and seat of the Ya Na since about 1700, when pressure from Gonja pushed the capital east. German forces burned it in 1896, and from 1899 it lay in German Togoland, passing to British…

yapahuwa.s: Yapahuwa is a rock fortress in the North Western Province of Sri Lanka that served as a royal capital in the late 13th century under Bhuvanaikabahu I. Its ornate stone staircase, decorated with lions, is its best-known feature.

york-minster.s: York Minster is the cathedral of York in northern England and the seat of the Archbishop of York. Its origins go back to the wooden church built for the baptism of King Edwin of Northumbria in 627, while the present Gothic building was constructed between about 1220 and 1472.

yorkshire.s: Yorkshire is a historic county of northern England, the largest in the country, stretching from the Pennines to the North Sea. It formed the core of the Anglian kingdom of Deira and later of the Viking Kingdom of York, whose settlers left hundreds of Scandinavian place-names.

yanan.s: Yan'an is a city in northern Shaanxi, China, on the Loess Plateau. After the Long March it was the headquarters of the Chinese Communist Party from 1937 to 1947, where Mao Zedong consolidated his leadership and the party developed its policies.

yuri-ii-boleslav.s: Yuri II Boleslav was the last ruler of the Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia, from 1323 until his death in 1340. Born Bolesław, a Masovian Piast prince whose mother was a daughter of Yuri I, he converted to Orthodoxy on taking the throne.

yemsa-language.s: Yemsa, formerly called Janjero, is an Omotic language of south-western Ethiopia, spoken by the Yem people in the hills east of the Omo river. It was the language of the Kingdom of Janjero, which was annexed to Menelik II's Ethiopian Empire in 1894.

yuknoom-cheen-ii.s: Yuknoom Ch'een II, also called Yuknoom the Great, was the most powerful king of the Kaan, or snake-head, dynasty at Calakmul, ruling from 636 to about 686. He fought Tikal, controlled the rulers of cities such as Dos Pilas, Cancuen and Naranjo, and made Calakmul the leading…

yigael-yadin.s: Yigael Yadin was an Israeli archaeologist, soldier and politician. Chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces from 1949 to 1952, he then led major excavations at Hazor in 1955–1958 and at Masada in 1963–1965 and published studies of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

yarim-lim-of-alalakh.s: Yarim-Lim was a prince of Yamhad and brother of King Abba-El I, who in the 18th century BCE received Alalakh and founded a dependent dynasty ruling the kingdom of Mukish under Aleppo. His palace at Alalakh was excavated by Leonard Woolley, and his descendants ruled until the…

yarim-lim-i.s: Yarim-Lim I was king of Yamhad, centred on Aleppo, in the early 18th century BCE, succeeding his father Sumu-Epuh. He resisted Shamshi-Adad I of Upper Mesopotamia and made Yamhad the leading power of Syria, allied with Zimri-Lim of Mari and Hammurabi of Babylon.

yaduraya.s: Yaduraya is the traditional founder of the Wodeyar dynasty of Mysore, said to have established himself as ruler there in 1399. According to dynastic accounts written much later, he and his brother came from the north, protected the local ruling family and married its princess.

yuksom.s: Yuksom is a village in western Sikkim, India, where in 1642 three Tibetan lamas consecrated Phuntsog Namgyal as the first Chogyal of Sikkim. It served as the kingdom's first capital until 1670, and the stone coronation throne of Norbugang survives there.

yakkha-sri-lanka.s: The Yakkhas are a people described in the Sri Lankan Pali chronicles as inhabitants of the island before the arrival of Prince Vijaya. In the legend Vijaya married the Yakkha woman Kuveni and later sent her away, and her children were said to have become the ancestors of the…

ynglings.s: The Ynglings were a legendary dynasty of Swedish kings at Uppsala, said to descend from the god Freyr. Their history is told in the poem Ynglingatal and in Snorri Sturluson's Ynglinga saga of the 13th century.

yadega.s: Yadega is the traditional founder of the Mossi kingdom of Yatenga in the north of present-day Burkina Faso, usually dated to the first half of the 16th century. Mossi tradition says that he was a prince of the Ouagadougou royal line who, passed over in a succession dispute,…

yelwa.s: Yelwa is a town in Kebbi State, north-western Nigeria, on the Niger river near the northern end of Kainji Lake. It became the capital of the Yauri kingdom in the 1880s and remains the seat of the Emir of Yauri.

yangon.s: Yangon, formerly Rangoon, is the largest city of Myanmar and was its capital until 2006. A small town around the Shwedagon Pagoda, it was renamed Yangon by King Alaungpaya in 1755.

yajurveda.s: The Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, the sacred texts of Hinduism, made up of prose formulas and verses recited by the adhvaryu priest as he performed the actions of the Vedic sacrifice. Compiled in the Kuru realm of northern India early in the 1st millennium BCE, it…

yevgeny-alekseyev.s: Yevgeny Alekseyev was a Russian admiral who commanded the Pacific Squadron and governed the Kwantung Oblast from Port Arthur, and in 1903 was appointed Viceroy of the Far East. His forceful policy in Manchuria and Korea helped bring on the Russo-Japanese War, in which he was…

yarang.s: Yarang is a district of Pattani province in southern Thailand, known for an extensive archaeological site of an early town. Excavations by Thailand's Fine Arts Department have uncovered moats, brick religious monuments and Buddhist votive tablets dating from about the 6th to…

yavne.s: Yavne is a town on the coastal plain of Israel, south of Jaffa, known in antiquity as Jamnia. After the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE it became a centre of rabbinic learning.

yennenga.s: Yennenga is a legendary princess of Mamprugu, honoured as the mother of the Mossi people of Burkina Faso. Tradition tells that she rode away from her father's court, met a hunter named Riale and bore a son, Ouedraogo, the founder of the Mossi kingdoms.

yasser-arafat.s: Yasser Arafat was the Palestinian nationalist leader who chaired the Palestine Liberation Organization from 1969 until his death and became the face of the Palestinian cause. A founder of Fatah in 1959, he pursued armed struggle and later negotiation, addressed the United…

yom-kippur-war.s: The Yom Kippur War was the surprise offensive of October 1973 in which Egypt and Syria sought to recover the lands lost in 1967, crossing the Suez Canal and storming the Golan Heights on the Day of Atonement. Israel recovered after early reverses and counter-attacked across…

yishuv.s: The Yishuv was the Jewish community in Palestine before the founding of Israel in 1948. Historians distinguish the Old Yishuv, the long-established religious communities of Jerusalem, Safed, Tiberias and Hebron, from the New Yishuv created by Zionist immigration from the 1880s.

yaruba-dynasty.s: The Yaruba dynasty ruled Oman from 1624 to 1742. Under Nasir ibn Murshid and his successors it united the country under Ibadi imams, drove the Portuguese from Muscat in 1650 and built a sea power that took Mombasa and other Swahili towns on the East African coast.

yeshaq-bahr-negash.s: Yeshaq was Bahr Negash, governor of the northern province of Medri Bahri in present-day Eritrea, in the mid-sixteenth century. He supported Emperor Gelawdewos against the Adal Sultanate but later rebelled and allied with the Ottomans of the Habesh Eyalet against the Ethiopian…

yumjaagiin-tsedenbal.s: Yumjaagiin Tsedenbal was the leader of the Mongolian People's Republic for over three decades, as head of the ruling party from 1940 to 1954 and from 1958 to 1984, and as prime minister from 1952 to 1974 and then head of state. Closely tied to the Soviet Union, he oversaw…

yoshida-koriyama-castle.s: Yoshida-Kōriyama Castle was a mountain castle in Aki province, now in Akitakata in Hiroshima Prefecture, the home base of the Mōri clan. Mōri Motonari successfully defended it against a large Amago army in 1540–1541, a victory that began his rise to power over western Japan.

yahya-muhammad-hamid-ed-din.s: Yahya Muhammad Hamid al-Din was the Zaydi imam of Yemen from 1904 and king of the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen from 1918 to 1948. He led the resistance to Ottoman rule, won autonomy by the Treaty of Daan in 1911, and took Sanaa when the Ottomans withdrew.

yazathingyan.s: Yazathingyan was the second of the three brothers who founded the Myinsaing regime in central Burma in the late 13th century. With Athinkhaya and Thihathu he governed the Kyaukse district, overthrew King Kyawswa of Pagan in 1297 and withstood a Yuan Mongol army in 1300 to 1301.

yushu-tibetan-autonomous-prefecture.s: Yushu is a Tibetan autonomous prefecture in southern Qinghai, China, covering high grasslands around the upper Yangtze and Mekong rivers. Historically part of the Tibetan region of Kham, it was the heartland of the kingdom of Nangchen and other Tibetan chiefdoms.

yangjumie.s: Yangjumie was the capital of the kingdom of Nanzhao from 779 and of its successors, including the Dali Kingdom, on the plain between the Cangshan mountains and Erhai Lake in Yunnan, China. It lay on the site of the old town of Dali.

yimouxun.s: Yimouxun was king of Nanzhao from 779 to 808. Early in his reign he joined Tibet in an invasion of Sichuan, but after a heavy defeat and growing Tibetan demands he returned to Tang allegiance in 794, swearing an oath with Tang envoys at Cangshan.

yungang-grottoes.s: The Yungang Grottoes are Buddhist cave temples near Datong in Shanxi province, China, carved mainly between about 460 and 494 under the Northern Wei, whose capital was then Pingcheng. Begun under the monk Tanyao after a persecution of Buddhism ended, they contain about 51,000…

yingchang.s: Yingchang was a city of the Yuan dynasty near Dali Lake in present-day Inner Mongolia, China, built by the Khongirad, the consort clan of the Mongol emperors. Toghon Temür, the last Yuan emperor, fled there after losing Dadu and Shangdu to the Ming and died there in 1370, and…

yangikent.s: Yangikent was a medieval town on the lower Syr Darya near the Aral Sea, in present-day Kazakhstan. In the 10th and 11th centuries it served as the winter capital of the Oghuz yabghu, the ruler of the Oghuz Turks, among their nomadic pastures.

yamandu-orsi.s: Yamandú Orsi is a Uruguayan politician of the left-wing Frente Amplio who became President of Uruguay on 1 March 2025. A former history teacher, he served two terms as intendant of Canelones Department from 2015 to 2024 before winning the 2024 presidential election in a run-off.

yamaguchi-city.s: Yamaguchi is a city in south-western Honshu, the capital of Yamaguchi Prefecture. In the 15th and 16th centuries it was the seat of the Ōuchi clan, who laid it out on the model of Kyoto and made it a centre of culture where the painter Sesshū worked and Francis Xavier preached…

yancai.s: Yancai was a nomadic people recorded in Chinese sources of the Han dynasty, living north-west of Kangju towards the Aral Sea and the Caspian. The Book of the Later Han states that the country was later renamed Alanliao, and many scholars link the Yancai with the Aorsi of Greek…

yamada-nagamasa.s: Yamada Nagamasa was a Japanese adventurer who settled in Ayutthaya in the early seventeenth century, led the Japanese community and its volunteer soldiers in the service of the Siamese kings, and won high rank at court. Drawn into the succession struggles that brought Prasat…

yu-deuk-gong.s: Yu Deuk-gong was a Korean scholar of the Silhak school in the late Joseon period, who served in the royal library under King Jeongjo. In his Balhaego, a study of the history of Balhae completed in 1784, he argued that Balhae and Unified Silla formed a period of Northern and…

yeta-iii.s: Yeta III was Litunga, king of the Lozi of Barotseland, from 1916 to 1945, succeeding his father Lewanika. Educated by missionaries, he tried to defend Barotseland's rights under British rule, petitioning the British government over the concessions and attending the coronation…

yehawmilk.s: Yehawmilk was a king of Byblos under the Achaemenid Persian Empire. His stele, found in 1869 and now in the Louvre, shows him in Persian dress before the enthroned goddess Baalat Gebal, and its Phoenician inscription records the buildings he dedicated to her.

yehimilk.s: Yehimilk was a king of Byblos in the tenth century BCE. His Phoenician inscription, discovered in 1930, records that he restored the ruined temples of the city and asks the gods to prolong his life.

ypres.s: Ypres (Ieper) is a city in West Flanders, Belgium. In the Middle Ages it was one of the three great cloth towns of the County of Flanders, with a vast Cloth Hall, and one of the Four Members of Flanders.

youth-pledge.s: The Youth Pledge (Sumpah Pemuda) was the declaration made on 28 October 1928 at the Second Indonesian Youth Congress in Batavia. Delegates of regional youth organisations pledged loyalty to one motherland, one nation and one language, Indonesian, adopting the Malay-based…

yahya-ibn-yahya-al-laythi.s: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi was a jurist of al-Andalus of Berber descent who studied in Medina under Malik ibn Anas and transmitted the most widely used version of Malik's al-Muwatta. Returning to Córdoba, he became the leading jurist of the emirate, influential under al-Hakam I…

yusuf-iv-of-granada.s: Yusuf IV, known as Ibn al-Mawl, was Nasrid emir of Granada for a few months in 1432. Backed by John II of Castile after the Castilian victory at La Higueruela, he took power from Muhammad IX and ruled as a Castilian vassal, but he soon lost support and was killed when Muhammad…

yen-the-insurrection.s: The Yên Thế Insurrection was a long rural resistance to French rule in the hill district of Yên Thế, north of Hanoi, which lasted from 1884 to 1913. Led for most of that time by Hoàng Hoa Thám, known as De Tham, the insurgents fought French columns and negotiated several…

yen-bai-mutiny.s: The Yên Bái mutiny was an uprising on the night of 9–10 February 1930 in which Vietnamese colonial soldiers at the garrison of Yên Bái in northern Vietnam, organised by the Vietnamese Nationalist Party, attacked their French officers. It was quickly suppressed; the French…

yamato-court.s: The Yamato court was the ruling power of early Japan, centred on the Yamato region around modern Nara, from which the Japanese imperial line descends. Between the third and seventh centuries it extended its authority over much of the archipelago and built the great…

yemaek.s: The Yemaek were an ancient people of southern Manchuria and northern Korea known from Chinese sources of the late first millennium BCE and the early centuries CE. They are regarded as the ancestors of the founders of Buyeo and Goguryeo and are often linked with the people of…

yeon-namsaeng.s: Yeon Namsaeng was the eldest son of the Goguryeo military dictator Yeon Gaesomun and succeeded him as the kingdom's chief minister. Soon after his father's death in 665 or 666 he was ousted by his younger brothers, fled to the fortress of Gungnae and went over to the Tang.

yeongnyu-of-goguryeo.s: Yeongnyu of Goguryeo was the twenty-seventh king of Goguryeo, reigning from 618 to 642. He sought peace with the newly founded Tang dynasty and exchanged prisoners from the Sui wars, while ordering a long defensive wall along the frontier.

yeondeunghoe.s: The Yeondeunghoe is a Korean Buddhist lantern festival. In the Goryeo kingdom it was a state festival held early in the year, at which lanterns were lit in honour of the Buddha, alongside the Palgwanhoe.

yi-ja-gyeom.s: Yi Ja-gyeom was a Korean aristocrat of the Gyeongwon Yi clan who dominated the Goryeo court in the early twelfth century. As father-in-law of two kings and grandfather of King Injong, he held enormous power.

yun-gwan.s: Yun Gwan was a Korean general and statesman of the Goryeo period. After defeats by the Jurchen he created the Byeolmuban, a special army, in 1104.

yuris-day.s: Yuri's Day, the autumn feast of St George on 26 November, was the time when Russian peasants were allowed to leave their landlords. The Sudebnik of 1497 limited peasant departure to the week before and the week after the feast, once the harvest was in and dues were settled.

yury-of-moscow.s: Yury of Moscow was prince of Moscow from 1303 and the first Moscow prince to hold the grand princely throne of Vladimir. Married to Konchaka, a sister of Uzbek Khan of the Golden Horde, he obtained the khan's patent in 1317 and fought the princes of Tver, whose ruler Mikhail…

yury-of-zvenigorod.s: Yury of Zvenigorod was a son of Dmitry Donskoy and prince of Zvenigorod and Galich. When his brother Vasily I died in 1425, he claimed the throne of Moscow against his nephew Vasily II under the old rule of succession from brother to brother, opening a long civil war.

yashahpala.s: Yashahpala was the last known ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, succeeding Trilochanapala in the early eleventh century, when the once great empire had dwindled to a small territory around Kannauj and Allahabad. His inscription of 1036 is the last record of the dynasty,…

yarim.s: Yarim is a town in the highlands of Yemen, in Ibb Governorate, about 2,600 metres above sea level on the road between Sanaa and Ibb. The ruins of Zafar, the capital of the Himyarite Kingdom, lie nearby, and the surrounding plateau was the Himyarite heartland.

yuan-haowen.s: Yuan Haowen was a poet, critic and historian of the Jin dynasty from Xinzhou in Shanxi, widely regarded as the greatest poet of northern China in his age. He served the Jin court and lived through its fall to the Mongols, which he lamented in his verse.

yi-hwang.s: Yi Hwang, known as Toegye, was one of the two greatest Neo-Confucian philosophers of Joseon Korea. After a career as an official he retired to teach at his academy at Dosan, near Andong.

yeonsangun-of-joseon.s: Yeonsangun was the tenth king of Joseon, ruling from 1494 to 1506, and is remembered as its worst tyrant. He carried out the literati purges of 1498 and 1504, the second in revenge for the death of his mother, who had been deposed and forced to take poison.

yi-i.s: Yi I, known as Yulgok, was one of the two greatest Neo-Confucian philosophers of Joseon Korea, alongside Yi Hwang. The son of the artist Sin Saimdang, he passed the civil service examinations at the top nine times and held high office.

yalangtush-bahadur.s: Yalangtush Bahadur was an Uzbek emir of the Alchin tribe who governed Samarkand for the Ashtarkhanid khans of Bukhara in the first half of the seventeenth century. A leading military commander of the khanate, he is said to have helped the Kazakh khan Jahangir against the…

yasovarman-i.s: Yasovarman I was king of the Khmer Empire from 889 to about 910. He moved the royal seat from Hariharalaya to the Angkor area, founding the city of Yasodharapura around the hill of Phnom Bakheng, which he crowned with his state temple, and built the great East Baray reservoir.

yser.s: The Yser is a river that rises in northern France and flows through West Flanders in Belgium to the North Sea at Nieuwpoort. In October 1914 the Belgian army halted the German advance on its banks, helped by opening the sluices at Nieuwpoort to flood the plain.

yoweri-museveni.s: Yoweri Museveni is a Ugandan politician and former rebel leader who has been President of Uganda since 1986. Born in Ankole, he fought against Idi Amin and then led the National Resistance Army in the Ugandan Bush War, which brought him to power.

yuhi-v-musinga.s: Yuhi V Musinga was king of Rwanda from 1896 to 1931. Brought to the throne as a youth by the Coup of Rucunshu, he ruled at first under the control of his mother Kanjogera and her kinsmen, and in 1897 accepted German protection.

yeha.s: Yeha is a town in the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia and the site of the oldest standing building in the country, the Great Temple, built around the seventh century BCE in South Arabian style. With other remains and Sabaean-style inscriptions, it shows close links with…

yaqaru.s: Yaqaru was the early, perhaps legendary, founder of the royal dynasty of Ugarit, probably in the first half of the second millennium BCE. Later kings of Ugarit still sealed royal documents with his old cylinder seal, the dynastic seal of the kingdom, and traced their line back…

yugoslav-committee.s: The Yugoslav Committee was a political body of South Slav exiles from Austria-Hungary, formally founded in London in 1915 and led by the Croatian politician Ante Trumbić. It lobbied the Allies for the union of the Habsburg South Slavs with Serbia, and in 1917 signed the Corfu…

yenangyaung.s: Yenangyaung is a town on the Irrawaddy in central Myanmar, whose name means stream of foul-smelling water. Hand-dug oil wells there were worked by hereditary families under royal licence in the Konbaung period, and from the late nineteenth century the Burmah Oil Company…

yaminites.s: The Yaminites (Binu Yamina, 'sons of the right', that is, of the south) were a confederation of Amorite pastoral tribes along the middle Euphrates in the early second millennium BCE. Known mainly from the Mari archives, they repeatedly resisted the kings of Mari, and Zimri-Lim…

yahdun-lim.s: Yahdun-Lim was an Amorite king of Mari around 1800 BCE. He subdued the pastoral tribes of the middle Euphrates, founded fortresses and led an expedition to the Mediterranean, where, according to his foundation inscription, he washed his weapons in the sea.

yaqui.s: The Yaqui are an Indigenous people of the Yaqui river valley in Sonora, north-western Mexico, with communities also in Arizona. For centuries they resisted Spanish and then Mexican control of their lands.

yongle-encyclopedia.s: The Yongle Encyclopedia was a vast Chinese compendium commissioned by the Yongle Emperor of the Ming dynasty and completed in 1408. More than 2,000 scholars compiled 22,877 chapters in over 11,000 volumes, copying earlier works on history, philosophy, literature, science and…

yusuf-ibn-al-hasan.s: Yusuf bin Hasan was a sultan of Mombasa, son of the ruler installed by the Portuguese, who was raised in Goa as a Christian under the name Dom Jerónimo Chingulia. Returning as sultan, he reverted to Islam and on 15 August 1631 killed the Portuguese garrison and residents of…

yelu-chucai.s: Yelü Chucai was a Khitan statesman of the Liao royal line who served Genghis Khan and Ögedei as adviser and administrator. He persuaded the Mongols to tax the conquered farmlands of northern China rather than turn them into pasture, organised a regular tax system with a…

yaroslavs-court.s: Yaroslav's Court is a historic area on the Trade Side of Veliky Novgorod, named after the palace of Yaroslav the Wise that once stood there. In the time of the Novgorod Republic it was the site of the main market and of the veche, the citizens' assembly, summoned by a bell.

yen-chia-kan.s: Yen Chia-kan was a Chinese economist and politician who served the Republic of China on Taiwan as finance minister, premier from 1963 to 1972 and vice-president from 1966. He succeeded Chiang Kai-shek as president on his death in 1975 and held office until 1978, when he…

yujiulu-chounu.s: Yujiulü Chounu was khagan of the Rouran from 508 to 520. He succeeded his father Futu, who had been killed by the Gaoche, and in 516 he defeated and killed the Gaoche king Mi'etu.

yujiulu-datan.s: Yujiulü Datan was khagan of the Rouran from 414 to 429. Soon after the death of the Northern Wei emperor Mingyuan in 423 he raided the Wei heartland around Shengle with a large cavalry army.

yujiulu-futu.s: Yujiulü Futu was khagan of the Rouran from 506 to 508. He fought the Gaoche, who had broken away from the Rouran in 487 and founded a kingdom in the west, and he was defeated and killed in battle by the Gaoche king Mi'etu in 508.

yujiulu-hulu.s: Yujiulü Hulü was khagan of the Rouran from 410 to 414, succeeding his brother Shelun, the founder of the khaganate. In 414 he was overthrown in a succession struggle within the royal clan, the first of many such disputes that weakened Rouran rule.

yujiulu-shelun.s: Yujiulü Shelun was the founder of the Rouran Khaganate. Driven north by the Northern Wei, he conquered the Gaoche tribes and other peoples of Mongolia and in 402 took the title khagan, with the regnal name Qiudoufa.

yakov-sverdlov.s: Yakov Sverdlov was a Bolshevik organiser and close associate of Lenin. From November 1917 he chaired the All-Russian Central Executive Committee, making him the formal head of state of Soviet Russia, while also running the party's secretariat.

yakuts.s: The Yakuts, who call themselves Sakha, are a Turkic people of north-eastern Siberia living mainly along the Lena River. They traditionally raised horses and cattle in a harsh subarctic climate and came under Russian rule in the seventeenth century.

yaeyama-islands.s: The Yaeyama Islands are the southernmost island group of Japan, in Okinawa Prefecture, lying east of Taiwan and including Ishigaki and Iriomote. Their chiefs were brought under the Ryukyu Kingdom after King Shō Shin defeated Oyake Akahachi in 1500.
