yajna-sri-satakarni.s: Yajna Sri Satakarni was one of the last powerful Satavahana kings, ruling in the late second century CE. He regained territory in the west from the Western Satraps, and his inscriptions and coins, including issues showing ships, come from both coasts of the Deccan.

yavana.s: Yavana is a term used in ancient Indian languages for Greeks and, later, for other westerners. Derived through Old Persian Yauna from 'Ionian', it appears in the edicts of Ashoka, in Sanskrit literature and in inscriptions recording gifts by Yavana donors to Buddhist caves of…

yinxu.s: Yinxu, the 'Ruins of Yin', is the site of the last capital of the Shang dynasty, near Anyang in Henan, China, occupied from about 1300 BCE until the Zhou conquest. Excavations since 1928 have revealed palace and temple foundations, royal tombs, bronze workshops, the tomb of Fu…

yazid-ibn-mazyad-al-shaybani.s: Yazid ibn Mazyad al-Shaybani was an Arab general and governor of the Abbasid Caliphate under Harun al-Rashid. He defeated the Kharijite rebel al-Walid ibn Tarif in 795 and served as governor of Armenia and Azerbaijan, which then included Shirvan.

yellow-sea.s: The Yellow Sea is the northern part of the East China Sea, between mainland China and the Korean peninsula. It takes its name from the yellow silt carried into it by the Yellow River.

yemeni-socialist-party.s: The Yemeni Socialist Party was founded in October 1978 when South Yemen's ruling National Liberation Front merged with smaller leftist groups. Organised on the Soviet model, it was the sole legal party of the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen until unification in 1990,…

yan-ying.s: Yan Ying, known as Yanzi, was a chief minister of the State of Qi who served Duke Ling, Duke Zhuang and Duke Jing in the sixth century BCE. He was famed for frugality, wit and frank advice to his rulers.

yingqiu.s: Yingqiu was the first capital of the State of Qi, according to the Shiji the seat granted to Jiang Ziya, Lord Taigong, when King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed him in the north of the Shandong peninsula. It is traditionally identified with Linzi, near present-day Zibo, which remained…

yom-river.s: The Yom River is a river of northern Thailand, rising in the Phi Pan Nam mountains of Phayao province and flowing south past Phrae and Sukhothai to join the Nan River in Nakhon Sawan province, part of the Chao Phraya basin. Its fertile valley supported the kingdom of…

yax-nuun-ayiin-i.s: Yax Nuun Ayiin I was a king of the Maya city of Tikal, installed as a boy in 379 after the arrival of Siyaj K'ak' and the death of King Chak Tok Ich'aak I. Inscriptions name his father as Spearthrower Owl, possibly a ruler of Teotihuacan, and he is depicted in…

yarlung-tsangpo.s: The Yarlung Tsangpo is the upper course of the Brahmaputra, flowing eastwards across southern Tibet for more than 1,000 km before cutting through the eastern Himalaya into India. Its valley and those of its tributaries, with Lhasa and Shigatse, have long been the agricultural…

yumten.s: Yumten was one of two claimants to the Tibetan throne after the death of the emperor Langdarma around 842, the other being his half-brother Ösung. Backed by a rival faction of the nobility, he is said to have held power in central Tibet around Lhasa while Ösung's line held…

yakutsk.s: Yakutsk is a city on the Lena River in eastern Siberia, founded as a cossack fort in 1632 by Pyotr Beketov. It became the main base for Russian exploration and fur-tribute collection in north-eastern Siberia, from which expeditions reached the Sea of Okhotsk and the Pacific.

yusuf-lule.s: Yusuf Lule was a Ugandan academic and politician who served as president of Uganda for 68 days in April–June 1979, after the overthrow of Idi Amin. A former principal of Makerere University College, he was chosen as leader of the Uganda National Liberation Front at the Moshi…

yugra.s: Yugra (Arabic Yura) was the medieval name for the lands and peoples of the far north-east of European Russia and north-western Siberia, around the northern Urals and the lower Ob. Arab writers describe the Yura as a people beyond the Wisu who sold furs to Bulgar merchants, and…

yunzhong-commandery.s: Yunzhong Commandery was a frontier commandery of the Qin and Han empires on the northern bend of the Yellow River, near modern Hohhot in Inner Mongolia. Founded by the state of Zhao and kept by its successors, it guarded the approaches from the Mongolian steppe and was a…

youliu-chanyu.s: Youliu was chanyu of the Northern Xiongnu in the late 1st century CE. In 87 CE he was killed by Xianbei warriors, who took his skin as a trophy.

yorkshire-wolds.s: The Yorkshire Wolds are low chalk hills in the East Riding of Yorkshire and North Yorkshire, England, curving from the Humber to the coast at Flamborough Head. Their well-drained soils have been farmed since prehistory, and they are rich in burial mounds, including the square…

yazdegerd-ii.s: Yazdegerd II was king of the Sasanian Empire of Persia from 438 to 457. He fought the Byzantines briefly and campaigned for years against the Kidarites and other Hunnic peoples on his north-eastern frontier.

york-river-virginia.s: The York River is a tidal estuary in eastern Virginia, formed by the junction of the Pamunkey and Mattaponi rivers and flowing about 55 kilometres into Chesapeake Bay. Werowocomoco, the seat of the Powhatan paramount chief, stood on its north bank, and Yorktown, where the…

yuryev-polsky.s: Yuryev-Polsky is a small town in Vladimir Oblast, Russia. Yuri Dolgoruky founded it in 1152 in the open fields, polye, between Vladimir and Pereslavl-Zalessky, and from 1212 it was the seat of a small appanage principality.

yaroslavl.s: Yaroslavl is a city on the Volga in Russia, north-east of Moscow, at the mouth of the Kotorosl. Founded in the early 11th century by Yaroslav the Wise, it was the seat of its own princes from 1218 until Moscow absorbed it in 1463.

yamacraw.s: The Yamacraw were a small Native American band formed in the 1720s by Creek and Yamasee people under Tomochichi, living at Yamacraw Bluff on the Savannah River. Their friendship with James Oglethorpe allowed the English to found Savannah there in 1733.

york-maine.s: York is a town on the southern coast of Maine, United States, settled by the English in the 1630s as Agamenticus. Sir Ferdinando Gorges chartered it in 1641 as the city of Gorgeana, the first chartered English city in America.

yamasee-war.s: The Yamasee War of 1715 to 1717 was a conflict between the Province of Carolina and the Yamasee, Muscogee and other Native peoples angered by the abuses of traders and by slave raiding. Attacks killed hundreds of settlers and traders and nearly destroyed the colony before an…

yazoo-river.s: The Yazoo River flows about 300 km through western Mississippi, United States, to join the Mississippi River just north of Vicksburg. In 1764 the latitude of its mouth was used to fix the northern boundary of British West Florida.

yun-bong-gil.s: Yun Bong-gil was a Korean independence activist and member of Kim Gu's Korean Patriotic Organisation. On 29 April 1932 he threw a bomb at a Japanese celebration in Hongkew Park, Shanghai, killing General Yoshinori Shirakawa and the head of the Japanese residents' association…

yasmah-addu.s: Yasmah-Addu was the younger son of Shamshi-Adad I, ruler of Upper Mesopotamia, who installed him as king of Mari on the middle Euphrates. Letters found at Mari show his father rebuking him for idleness while praising his elder brother Ishme-Dagan at Ekallatum.

yauta.s: Yauta (Uaite') was a king of the Qedarite Arabs in the 7th century BCE, son of Hazael. Esarhaddon of Assyria confirmed him as king and returned the images of his gods in exchange for extra tribute, but he later joined the revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin of Babylon against…

yang-dipertuan-muda.s: Yang Dipertuan Muda ('junior ruler') was the title of the viceroy or under-king of the Johor-Riau and later Riau-Lingga sultanates. From 1722 the office was held hereditarily by Bugis nobles, who controlled government and trade from the island of Penyengat while the Malay…

york-factory.s: York Factory was a fur-trading post of the Hudson's Bay Company at the mouth of the Hayes River on Hudson Bay, in today's Manitoba. Founded in 1684, it was for two centuries the company's main depot, where Cree and other traders brought furs and goods were shipped to and from…

yamamoto-tsunetomo.s: Yamamoto Tsunetomo was a samurai of the Saga domain in Kyushu who served the Nabeshima lord Mitsushige. When his lord died in 1700 and retainers were forbidden to follow him in death, he became a Buddhist monk and retired to a hermitage.

yining.s: Yining, known in Uyghur as Ghulja, is a city in the Ili valley of north-western Xinjiang, China, near the border with Kazakhstan. In the Qing period it was a trading town of the Ili region, which Russia occupied from 1871 to 1881.

yap-ah-loy.s: Yap Ah Loy was a Hakka Chinese tin-mining leader who became Kapitan Cina of Kuala Lumpur in 1868. During the Klang War he backed the Sultan's viceroy, Tengku Kudin, and he rebuilt Kuala Lumpur after it was destroyed in the fighting and again after fire and flood.

yonne-river.s: The Yonne is a river of central France, about 290 km long, rising in the Morvan and joining the Seine at Montereau. It flows past Auxerre and Sens and gives its name to a department of Burgundy.

yazidis.s: The Yazidis are a Kurdish-speaking religious community of northern Iraq, north-east Syria, south-east Turkey and the Caucasus, whose monotheistic faith centres on God and seven holy beings led by Melek Taus, the Peacock Angel. Their holiest shrine is at Lalish, the tomb of the…

yu-county-hebei.s: Yu County, or Yuxian, is a county in Zhangjiakou in north-western Hebei province, China, in an upland basin near the Shanxi border. It occupies the area of ancient Dai, a state of the Di peoples conquered by Zhao in the fifth century BCE, and later the seat of the kingdoms and…

ying-chu.s: Ying was the capital of the State of Chu for most of its history, usually identified with the walled site of Ji'nancheng near modern Jingzhou in Hubei. King Wen of Chu moved the capital there in the seventh century BCE, though its early location is debated.

yongcheng.s: Yongcheng, or Yong, was the capital of the State of Qin from 677 to 383 BCE, near modern Fengxiang in western Shaanxi. Excavations have revealed its walls, palace and temple foundations and the great tomb attributed to Duke Jing of Qin, the largest pre-imperial tomb excavated…

yangzhou.s: Yangzhou is a city in central Jiangsu, on the north bank of the Yangtze where the Grand Canal meets the river. As Jiangdu it was the favourite southern residence of Emperor Yang of Sui, who was murdered there in 618.

yeshaq-i.s: Yeshaq I was emperor of Ethiopia from 1414 to 1429, a son of Dawit I of the Solomonic dynasty. He fought the Muslim states to the east, and some accounts place the death of Sultan Sa'ad ad-Din II of Ifat near Zeila in his reign.

yusuf-mahamud-ibrahim.s: Yusuf Mahamud Ibrahim was sultan of the Geledi in southern Somalia in the first half of the 19th century and the most powerful ruler of the Gobroon dynasty. From Afgooye he dominated the lower Shabelle valley and influenced the Benadir ports, and in 1843 he led a large army…

yadava.s: The Yadavas are an ancient lineage of Indian tradition, descended from the legendary king Yadu. In the Mahabharata and the Puranas they are the clans of Mathura and Dwarka to which Krishna belonged.

yamuna.s: The Yamuna is a major river of northern India and the largest tributary of the Ganges, flowing about 1,370 kilometres from the Himalaya past Delhi, Mathura and Agra to join the Ganges at Prayagraj. The fertile Ganga–Yamuna doab between the two rivers was the heartland of many…

yesugei.s: Yesügei was a chief of the Borjigin clan of the Mongols and the father of Temüjin, later Genghis Khan. He fought the Tatars and was a sworn brother of the Keraite ruler Toghrul.

yamunotri.s: Yamunotri is a Hindu pilgrimage site in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand, India, near the source of the Yamuna river in the western Garhwal Himalaya. Its temple to the goddess Yamuna and nearby hot springs make it the first stop of the Char Dham pilgrimage, which…

yax-ehb-xook.s: Yax Ehb Xook was the founder of the royal dynasty of Tikal, the Maya city in northern Guatemala, as recorded by its later kings, who counted their place in the succession from him. He is thought to have lived in the 1st century CE, traditionally around 90, and one of the early…

yonago.s: Yonago is a city in western Tottori Prefecture, Japan, on the Sea of Japan coast near the border with Shimane, in the former province of Hoki. Its castle, completed in the early 17th century, was held under the Tottori domain by the Arao family, senior retainers of the Ikeda…

yanagawa-affair.s: The Yanagawa affair was a dispute in Japan in the 1630s. Yanagawa Shigeoki, a senior retainer of the Sō lords of Tsushima, revealed that the Sō had forged and altered diplomatic letters exchanged between the Tokugawa shoguns and the kings of Joseon Korea in order to restore…

yemelyan-pugachev.s: Yemelyan Pugachev was a Don Cossack who in 1773 claimed to be the murdered Emperor Peter III and led the largest Cossack and peasant rising in Russian history against Catherine the Great. Backed by Yaik Cossacks, Bashkirs, factory serfs and peasants, his forces burned Kazan…

yashaskara.s: Yashaskara was a king of Kashmir, chosen by an assembly of Brahmins in 939 after years of strife among the palace guards and court factions that had followed the Utpala dynasty's decline. Kalhana's Rajatarangini presents him as a just ruler who restored order.

ynglinga-saga.s: Ynglinga saga is the first part of Heimskringla, the history of the kings of Norway written in Old Norse by the Icelander Snorri Sturluson around 1230. It traces the legendary Yngling dynasty from the god Odin through the kings of Uppsala to the petty kings of Vestfold,…

yajnavalkya.s: Yajnavalkya was a Vedic sage of Videha, regarded as the teacher of the White Yajurveda and the source of the Shatapatha Brahmana. In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad he wins the philosophical contest at King Janaka's court and teaches that the self, atman, is identical with brahman.

yuri-ii-of-vladimir.s: Yuri II Vsevolodovich was grand prince of Vladimir from 1212 to 1216 and again from 1218 to 1238, a son of Vsevolod the Big Nest. In 1221 he founded Nizhny Novgorod as a base against Volga Bulgaria.

yinchuan.s: Yinchuan is the capital of the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region in north-western China, on the Yellow River plain below the Helan Mountains. Under the name Xingqing it was the capital of the Western Xia empire of the Tanguts from 1038 until the Mongol conquest of 1227.

yuwen-huaji.s: Yuwen Huaji (died 619) was a Sui dynasty general who in 618 led the coup at Jiangdu (modern Yangzhou) in which Emperor Yang of Sui was strangled. He marched his army north and proclaimed himself emperor of a state called Xu, but was defeated by Li Mi and then captured by Dou…

yaka-people.s: The Yaka are a Bantu-speaking people of the Kwango valley in the south-west of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and in northern Angola. In the 18th century Lunda warriors conquered them and founded a Yaka kingdom ruled by kings titled kiamfu.

yang-guozhong.s: Yang Guozhong (died 756) was chancellor of Tang China under Emperor Xuanzong and a cousin of the emperor's favourite consort, Yang Guifei. His rivalry with the general An Lushan helped provoke An's rebellion in 755.

youzhou.s: Youzhou was a historical prefecture of northern China centred on the city of Ji, on the site of modern Beijing. A frontier stronghold against the steppe peoples, it was the base of the Tang general An Lushan and later of the warlord Liu Rengong and his son's short-lived Yan…

yarkand.s: Yarkand, also called Shache, is an oasis city in the south-western Tarim Basin of Xinjiang, China, on the Yarkand River. A station on the Silk Road routes to India and Bactria, it was the capital of the Yarkent Khanate from 1514 until the Dzungar conquest of 1680, and later a…

yaxuun-bahlam-iv.s: Yaxuun B'ahlam IV, known as Bird Jaguar IV, was king of the Maya city of Yaxchilan from 752 to about 768 and a son of Itzamnaaj B'ahlam III. He came to the throne ten years after his father's death and used many carved monuments to assert his right to rule.

yopaat-bahlam-i.s: Yopaat B'ahlam I was the founder of the royal dynasty of the Maya city of Yaxchilan, who according to later inscriptions took power in 359 CE. Later kings counted their place in the succession from him, and 8th-century lintels and a hieroglyphic stairway list the dynasty's…

yeke-people.s: The Yeke are a people of the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, descended from the Nyamwezi traders and followers who came from western Tanzania with Msiri in the mid-19th century. They formed the ruling core of Msiri's kingdom at Bunkeya, and after his…

yunnan.s: Yunnan is a province of south-western China bordering Myanmar, Laos and Vietnam, with Kunming as its capital. Its plateau was the base of the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms until the Mongol conquest of 1253, after which it was ruled as a province of China.

yenisei-river.s: The Yenisei is one of the great rivers of Siberia, flowing north from the mountains of Tuva and Mongolia through central Russia to the Kara Sea of the Arctic Ocean. Its upper valley, in the Minusinsk Basin and Tuva, was the homeland of the Yenisei Kyrgyz, who left Old Turkic…

yamagata-prefecture.s: Yamagata Prefecture is a prefecture in the Tōhoku region of northern Honshu, Japan, with the city of Yamagata as its capital. It was formed from the former Dewa Province and the domains of the area, among them Yonezawa and Shōnai, after the abolition of the han system in 1871,…

yufir-ibn-abd-al-rahman-al-hiwali.s: Yu'fir ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hiwali was a Yemeni chief of the Himyarite Hiwal tribe who founded the Yufirid dynasty in the 9th century. Around 847 he seized the highland fortress of Shibam Kawkaban and soon took Sanaa from the Abbasid governors, ruling much of the Yemeni…

yarlung-valley.s: The Yarlung Valley is a valley south of the Yarlung Tsangpo river in Lhoka, south-central Tibet, around the town of Tsetang. It was the home of the line of chiefs who united Tibet in the seventh century and founded the Tibetan Empire, and the neighbouring Chongye valley holds…

yemeni-civil-war-2014-present.s: The Yemeni civil war began in 2014 when the Houthi movement seized Sanaa and then forced President Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi from power. In 2015 a coalition led by Saudi Arabia intervened in support of the government.

yung-wing.s: Yung Wing was a Chinese-American diplomat and businessman who in 1854 became the first recorded Chinese graduate of an American university, Yale College. In 1863 Zeng Guofan sent him to the United States to buy machinery, which went into the Jiangnan Arsenal at Shanghai.
